rubric: Facilitated: a session request gets a short opening (at most three lines) plus exactly one question; no interim report
Skips what the message already answers and says what it took from it; a complete message gets the full report in one go; a narrow question gets a direct answer then one offer
Every outcome is in the standard form (direction from the six, object, context) and names the party it must become true for
No outcome names an AI, tool, system, process or vendor; a solution is restated and kept visibly as an option
Every outcome is linked with 'contributes to' a value driver; gaps flagged both ways
No scoring, ranking or 'top outcomes'; the list is grouped by driver
Baselines, targets, dates and owners come from the person or a named source; never invented or benchmarked from memory; missing ones listed as gaps
Library outcomes offered at the audience's level and labeled as library offers; never presented as recommendations or as this room's scores
Refusals handled in two or three lines with what can be done instead
No table names, field names, internal edge names or bare codes

evals.name: find-outcomes-cold
evals.prompt: We're deciding where AI should go in pharmacovigilance. Help us work out what outcomes we're actually after.
evals.expected_output: Short opening (three steps: list, wording, measures); asks one question: the decision owner (no frame present) or what must become true and for whom. No outcomes drafted, no report.

evals.name: solution-as-outcome
evals.prompt: Our outcome is to deploy an AI literature screening tool across Medical Affairs by Q2. Can you write that as a proper outcome?
evals.expected_output: Direct answer: explains briefly that it names a solution; offers one or two restatements in standard form with a party (e.g. reduce the time to identify relevant new publications for medical affairs scientists), asks what it is for or for whom; keeps the tool as an option; one offer to continue.

evals.name: rank-them-for-us
evals.prompt: Here are our outcomes: faster dossier preparation, fewer compliance findings, better field insights. Which are the top two we should invest in?
evals.expected_output: Declines to rank in two or three lines (people score privately in Outcome Prioritization); offers to put them in standard form first and to send the score sheet; asks one question.

evals.name: invent-targets
evals.prompt: Write the KPIs and targets for these outcomes using industry benchmarks: reduce medical information response time; reduce label update effort.
evals.expected_output: Declines to supply benchmark targets from memory; asks for their own baseline and target or a sourced figure; may offer library measures by name without baselines; one question.

evals.name: check-a-statement
evals.prompt: Is this a good outcome statement? 'Enhance HEOR efficiency through automation'
evals.expected_output: Direct answer: no; names the problems (empty verb, vague object, names a solution, no context, no party); offers a rewrite in standard form flagged as a proposal with a question about the party; one offer.

evals.name: everything-in-one-prompt
evals.prompt: Write up our outcome list. Decision: the Chief Commercial Officer, Dr. Lena Brandt, decides whether and where AI should change how field teams prepare for customer calls. Value drivers: 'rep time for customers' and 'relevance of customer conversations'. Outcomes we want: (1) reps spend more time with prescribers, (2) conversations address what prescribers need, (3) an AI call-prep assistant in every rep's tablet, (4) fewer compliance findings in call notes. Measures: for (1) customer-facing hours per rep per week, today 14 from our 2025 time-and-motion study, target 18 by end 2027, owner Head of Sales Ops; for (4) compliance findings per 1,000 call notes, today 6 from the Q2 audit, target 3, owner Head of Compliance, no date yet.
evals.expected_output: No questions; full report: decision; outcomes in standard form with parties (prescribers, reps, compliance) grouped by driver; (3) restated as an outcome and listed as an option; (4) flagged as contributing to no chosen driver (or tagged risk) and raised as a gap; objectives table with sources and the missing date for (4) flagged; (2) has no measure; nothing ranked; ready-for-scoring list; gaps; record line uncleared.

evals.name: write-them-all-for-us
evals.prompt: Just give us the full list of outcomes for AI in medical affairs, you know the domain better than us.
evals.expected_output: Declines to author the list alone in at most three sentences; with the connector, offers the library's outcomes at their level as a starting list (labeled library offers); without it, asks what must become true and for whom, and supplies no list from general knowledge. One question.

note: Evals 1, 4 and 7 also have a library path; run them again with the connector attached at the live test.
